import HartshorneLib.Chapter4IntrinsicResidue

/-!
# The global residue theorem for exact differentials

The intrinsic residue of an exact rational differential vanishes at every
closed point.  Summing the pointwise vanishing gives the global residue
theorem for the exact subspace without introducing a global trace map.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory AlgebraicGeometry

namespace Hartshorne

noncomputable section

attribute [local instance] functionFieldOverAlgebra stalkOverAlgebra
  stalkFunctionFieldOver_isScalarTower

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
variable (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsIntegral X.left]
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 X.hom]

/-! The pointwise exactness result also packages the support needed by later
trace constructions. -/

theorem curveRationalDifferentialResidue_differential_support_empty
    (f : X.left.functionField) :
    Function.support (fun p : {x : X.left // x ≠ genericPoint X.left} =>
      curveRationalDifferentialResidue X p.2
        (KaehlerDifferential.D k X.left.functionField f)) = ∅ := by
  ext p
  simp [curveRationalDifferentialResidue_differential]

/-- The sum of intrinsic residues of an exact rational differential is zero. -/
theorem finsum_curveRationalDifferentialResidue_differential_eq_zero
    (f : X.left.functionField) :
    (∑ᶠ p : {x : X.left // x ≠ genericPoint X.left},
      curveRationalDifferentialResidue X p.2
        (KaehlerDifferential.D k X.left.functionField f)) = 0 := by
  classical
  calc
    _ = ∑ᶠ p : {x : X.left // x ≠ genericPoint X.left}, 0 :=
      finsum_congr fun p => curveRationalDifferentialResidue_differential X p.2 f
    _ = 0 := finsum_zero

end
end Hartshorne
